inputs.name: case_folded_key
inputs.description: A JSON key in the request body or in a bidder response matches a field of the Go type only when case is ignored (`ID` for `id`).

inputs.name: deep_nesting
inputs.description: A JSON document in the request body or in a bidder response nests 128 levels or more, its outermost value included.

inputs.name: duplicate_keys
inputs.description: A JSON object in the request body or in a bidder response has the same key twice.

inputs.name: invalid_utf8
inputs.description: A JSON string in the request body or in a bidder response holds bytes that are not UTF-8.

inputs.name: options_request
inputs.description: The request's method is OPTIONS: a CORS preflight, or any other OPTIONS, which tower-http's CorsLayer answers as one.

differences.title: Large stored-data entries: freecache refuses them, moka keeps them
differences.go: freecache refuses an entry whose key and value together are longer than 1/1024 of the cache less its 24-byte entry header (`ErrLargeEntry`, whose text says only 1/1024; freecache's segment.go:73-76): a 1 MiB cache keeps a 993-byte document under a 7-byte key, 1000 bytes in all, and refuses a 994-byte one. Prebid logs the error and drops the entry (stored_requests/caches/memory/maps.go:60-64), so such a document is fetched again on every request.
differences.rust: moka, bounded by the same byte budget through a weigher, keeps every entry that fits the budget.
differences.visible_in: Fetches and error logs of the stored request, imp, response and account caches when a document is larger than 1/1024 of its in-memory cache

differences.title: Boolean `PBS_` variables: Viper converts them with `cast.ToBool`, the config crate with its own spellings
differences.go: For a key with a bool default, Viper converts a `PBS_` value with `cast.ToBool` (`SetTypeByDefaultValue`, config/config.go:1319), which is `strconv.ParseBool` with its error dropped: `1`, `t`, `T`, `true`, `TRUE` and `True` are true, and every other value (`tRuE`, `yes`, `YES`, `on`, `y`, `maybe` and the false forms) is false, never an error. A key bound only with `BindEnv` goes through mapstructure's weak decode: `ParseBool`, the empty string is false, and anything else fails the load (orchestrator ruling 8).
differences.rust: The config crate takes `1`, `true`, `on` and `yes` and their false forms (`0`, `false`, `off`, `no`) in any case, and fails the load on `t`, `T`, `f`, `F`, `y`, `n` and `maybe`.
differences.visible_in: Startup with `PBS_` environment variables that set boolean keys
differences.restore: CONFIG-LOADER converts as Viper does: `cast.ToBool` for keys with a bool default, and mapstructure's weak decode for keys bound only with `BindEnv` (`adapters.<bidder>.disabled`, `.debug.allow`, `.experiment.adsCert.enabled`, `.modifyingVastXmlAllowed`, `account_defaults.privacy.dsa.gdpr_only` and the others the defaults table marks), each path against a Go golden of its own (orchestrator ruling 8).

differences.title: Environment variable names: Viper reads `PBS_` and the upper-case key and the `BindEnv` fallbacks, the config crate its own mapping
differences.go: Viper reads `PBS_` and the key upper-cased with `.` replaced by `_`, by its exact name (config/config.go:1318-1321), and the un-prefixed name of each key bound before the prefix is set (`GDPR_DEFAULT_VALUE` and four others, config/config.go:1167-1168, 1192 and 1258-1259); an empty variable is unset, and a variable set for a section hides the keys under it.
differences.rust: The config crate's `Environment` source with the prefix `PBS` and `_` as the separator matches names in any case, makes every `_` a level (`PBS_GDPR_DEFAULT_VALUE` sets `gdpr.default.value`), reads no name without the prefix and keeps an empty value.
differences.visible_in: Startup with `PBS_` or fallback environment variables
differences.restore: CONFIG-LOADER reads, from a snapshot of the environment, the variables Viper reads by their exact names, with the fallbacks of the defaults table, and drops empty ones.

differences.title: Config decode errors: mapstructure's words, with values printed as Rust prints them
differences.go: `config.New` wraps mapstructure's error as `viper failed to unmarshal app config: ...` (config/config.go:758-760) and main.go:42 logs it fatally: mapstructure lists every field that fails, sorted, as `2 error(s) decoding:` and lines such as `* cannot parse 'account_defaults.cookie_sync.max_limit' as int: strconv.ParseInt: parsing "\u00a0x": invalid syntax`, printing values with fmt's `%v` (`[1e+06 1e-05]`) and quoting strings with `strconv.Quote`.
differences.rust: The loader gives the same wrapper and the same failures in the same order and words, but prints a float as Rust spells it (`[1000000 0.00001]`), quotes a string as Rust quotes it (`"\u{a0}x"`), and lists the keys of a `map[interface{}]interface{}` value in the order of their text.
differences.visible_in: The startup error for a configuration whose values do not decode into `config.Configuration`, where a value it prints holds a float Go prints with an exponent, a character `strconv.Quote` escapes otherwise than Rust, or a map whose keys are not strings
differences.restore: Port fmt's `%v` and `strconv.Quote` with Go's Unicode tables; not planned (orchestrator ruling 2 ledgers library error wording).
differences.note: The wrapper is Prebid's text and stays exact (`error_wrapper_exact`), and the other decode errors of `loads.json`, `matrix.json` and `scalars.json` are Go's texts but for the quoting of the one `scalars.json` input holding U+00A0 and U+2003 (`weak_decode_matches_mapstructure`).

differences.title: Booleans in pbs.yaml: Viper converts yaml.v3's untyped value with `cast.ToBool`, the config crate takes serde-saphyr's
differences.go: Viper takes a pbs.yaml value as yaml.v3 resolves it untyped (`true`, `True`, `TRUE` and their false forms are booleans, `yes`, `on`, `y` and `tRuE` stay strings, `1` is a number) and converts it with `cast.ToBool` for a key with a bool default, so `true`, `True`, `t` and `1` are true, and `yes`, `on`, `y`, `tRuE`, `maybe` and every false form are false, never an error.
differences.rust: Through serde-saphyr and the config crate, `yes`, `on`, `y` and `tRuE` are true, `n`, `no` and `off` are false, and `t`, `f` and `maybe` fail the load.
differences.visible_in: Startup with a pbs.yaml that sets a boolean key
differences.restore: CONFIG-LOADER converts pbs.yaml values as Viper does: `cast.ToBool` after yaml.v3's untyped resolution (orchestrator ruling 8).

differences.title: The config file: Viper reads the first `pbs.<ext>` of its search, the config crate merges every file source
differences.go: Viper looks in `.` and then in `/etc/config` for `pbs.<ext>` in its extension order (`json` before `toml`), skipping a directory, reads the first file found and no other, and ignores a file that does not parse (config/config.go:936-940 and 1322).
differences.rust: The config crate reads every file source it is given and merges them, tries its own formats in its order at each (`toml` before `json`), and fails the build on a file that does not parse.
differences.visible_in: Startup with config files in both directories, with more than one `pbs.<ext>`, or with one that does not parse
differences.restore: CONFIG-LOADER searches as Viper does and reads the one file found, keeping its parse error and the defaults when it does not parse.

differences.title: Config file formats: Viper reads twelve extensions, the loader JSON, TOML and YAML
differences.go: Viper looks for `pbs.<ext>` in `.` and then in `/etc/config` over `json`, `toml`, `yaml`, `yml`, `properties`, `props`, `prop`, `hcl`, `tfvars`, `dotenv`, `env` and `ini` (viper.go:419, viper_go1_15.go:16-45) and reads the first file found with that format's reader (config/config.go:936-940).
differences.rust: The loader searches the same way and reads JSON, TOML and YAML; when the first file found is in another format, the load fails with an error that names the file and the formats it reads.
differences.visible_in: Startup with a pbs.properties, pbs.props, pbs.prop, pbs.hcl, pbs.tfvars, pbs.dotenv, pbs.env or pbs.ini that Viper would read
differences.restore: Port the remaining readers (magiconair/properties, hashicorp/hcl, subosito/gotenv and gopkg.in/ini.v1); not planned.

differences.title: pbs.json: encoding/json reads documents serde_json refuses, and the two word their errors each their own way
differences.go: Viper reads pbs.json with encoding/json into `map[string]interface{}`, every number a `float64`: invalid UTF-8 and a lone surrogate escape each become U+FFFD, and 200 levels of nesting read (encoding/json takes 10000). A file that does not parse is ignored with encoding/json's error (`unexpected end of JSON input`), which Prebid drops (config/config.go:1322).
differences.rust: The loader reads pbs.json with serde_json, every number a `float64` too: a document holding invalid UTF-8 or a lone surrogate escape, or nesting 128 levels or more, does not parse, so the file is ignored and the defaults stay; a file neither reads is ignored with serde_json's error (`EOF while parsing an object at line 1 column 13`).
differences.visible_in: Startup with a pbs.json that holds invalid UTF-8 or a lone surrogate escape, or nests 128 levels or more: its settings are not applied
differences.restore: Rewrite lone surrogate escapes with pbs-jsonutil's `replace_lone_surrogates` before serde_json reads the file (orchestrator ruling 7), once pbs-config's base holds pbs-jsonutil; invalid UTF-8 and the depth stay as D-DECODE leaves them for requests (json.invalid-utf8, json.nesting-depth).
differences.note: json.lone-surrogates restores lone surrogates where Go decodes request-time input; this unit's base predates the JSONUTIL merge that holds the rewrite.

differences.title: Config keys: Viper lower-cases them, the config crate keeps file keys as written
differences.go: Viper lower-cases every key, so `Port:`, `port:` and `PORT:` in pbs.yaml all set `port`.
differences.rust: The config crate keeps file keys as written: only `port:` sets `port`, and the other spellings are ignored, so the default stays.
differences.visible_in: Startup with a pbs.yaml whose keys are not in lower case
differences.restore: CONFIG-LOADER lower-cases file and environment keys, as Viper does.

restorations.note: `strings.ToLower`, `strings.ToUpper` and `strings.EqualFold` of non-ASCII keys, against Go's own results.

differences.title: Key case: Go maps letters by Unicode 15.0.0, the loader by std's later Unicode tables
differences.go: Viper lower-cases the keys of the configuration file and upper-cases the `PBS_` names with `strings.ToLower` and `strings.ToUpper` (viper.go insensitiviseMap and mergeWithEnvPrefix, v1.12.0), and mapstructure matches keys to fields with `strings.EqualFold`; go1.26.2's tables are Unicode 15.0.0's, so a letter whose case pair a later version added, such as U+A7CB, U+10D50 or U+1C89, stays as it is.
differences.rust: The loader maps each character by its simple mapping as Go does, from std's tables, which are a later Unicode version's: those letters map to their pairs (U+A7CB to U+0264, U+10D50 to U+10D70, U+1C89 to U+1C8A).
differences.visible_in: A key of the configuration file, such as a module's setting under `hooks.modules`, that holds a letter Unicode gave a case pair after 15.0.0
differences.restore: Carry Unicode 15.0.0's case tables for keys; not planned.

differences.title: Layers: Viper resolves each key over the defaults, the file and the environment, the config crate merges its sources into one tree
differences.go: Viper's `Get` takes a key from the environment, then the file, then the defaults (viper.go:1220-1354): a `null` file value leaves the default (`port: ~` keeps 8000), and a dotted key inside a section sets the key under it (`gdpr:` with `tcf2.enabled: false` sets `gdpr.tcf2.enabled`).
differences.rust: The config crate merges its sources into one tree, a later source's value replacing an earlier one at its path, so a `null` replaces the default and fails the read; a dotted key below the top level is a key of its own, so the default stays.
differences.visible_in: Startup with a configuration that has `null` values or dotted keys inside sections, or `PBS_` variables for sections
differences.restore: CONFIG-LOADER resolves each key as Viper's `find`, `IsSet`, `AllKeys` and `AllSettings` do and decodes Viper's tree.

restorations.note: Every load of `loads.json`, the layering ones among them.

differences.title: Map order in the config tree: Go's varies from run to run, the loader's is sorted
differences.go: Where `AllSettings` writes a key and a key under it (a file value under a key with a default, such as `port:` with `a: 1` below it, or `{a: 1}` for a list key) or a `null` file section with `PBS_` variables under it, the tree it builds and the decode of it depend on the order Go iterates a map in, which varies from run to run (viper.go:1940-1957 and 2021-2038). So does the vendor the account modules hook names when several modules do not marshal (config/account_module_decoder.go:16-50).
differences.rust: The loader takes the keys in sorted order, which gives one of Go's outcomes, the same on every run.
differences.visible_in: Startup with a configuration that gives a key a value and keys under it, or a null section with `PBS_` variables under it, and the startup error for account modules of which several do not marshal
differences.restore: None: any one order is an order Go can take.

differences.title: Account module config bytes: jsonutil.Marshal escapes HTML and spells floats as strconv does, serde_json writes its own way
differences.go: `AccountModulesHookFunc` marshals each module's configuration with `jsonutil.Marshal` into a `json.RawMessage` (config/account_module_decoder.go:16-61): keys sorted, `<`, `>` and `&` as `\u003c`, `\u003e` and `\u0026`, and floats as strconv spells them: `3` for 3.0, `100000000000000000000` for 1e20, `1e-07` and `-0` (`1e+21` as serde_json writes it).
differences.rust: The loader writes the bytes with serde_json: keys sorted, and a whole float that fits an i64 or a u64 as the integer Go writes (`3`, `12345678901234567000`), but the characters as they are and the other floats in serde_json's spelling (`1e+20`, `1e-7`); -0 is `0`.
differences.visible_in: Only the bytes a module receives for `account_defaults.hooks.modules`: a module that parses them reads the same values
differences.restore: Write the bytes with Go's escaping and float spelling, which json.html-escape and json.float-format leave as they are; not planned.

differences.title: pbs.toml dates and times: go-toml gives Go time types, the toml crate their text
differences.go: Viper reads pbs.toml with go-toml v2.0.1: an offset date-time is a `time.Time` and a local date, time or date-time go-toml's `LocalDate`, `LocalTime` or `LocalDateTime`, which mapstructure refuses for a string field (`expected type 'string', got unconvertible type 'time.Time'`) and the account modules hook writes as JSON. A file that does not parse is ignored, with go-toml's error text, which Prebid drops (config/config.go:1322).
differences.rust: The config crate's TOML reader (the toml crate) gives every date and time as its TOML text, which a string field takes. A file that does not parse is ignored as in Go, with the toml crate's error text.
differences.visible_in: Startup with a pbs.toml that holds a date or time value
differences.restore: Port go-toml v2.0.1's date and time types; not planned.

differences.title: Config values into typed fields: Viper casts by the default's type and mapstructure decodes weakly, the config crate converts by the type serde asks for
differences.go: Viper casts a value with spf13/cast by the type of the key's default (`SetTypeByDefaultValue`, config/config.go:1319), dropping cast's error, and `v.Unmarshal` decodes the tree with mapstructure's `WeaklyTypedInput` and `AccountModulesHookFunc` (config/config.go:758): `0x10` is 16, `4x2` is 0 for a key with a default, 4.5 is 4, a scalar is a one-element list, a list of maps merges into a map, and a number is cut to the field's size.
differences.rust: The config crate converts by the type serde asks for: a string into a number in decimal only (`0x10` and `4x2` fail the load), a float into an integer rounded (4.5 is 5), and never a scalar into a list.
differences.visible_in: Startup with a pbs.yaml, pbs.json, pbs.toml or `PBS_` variables whose values are not of the field's type
differences.restore: CONFIG-LOADER ports cast's conversions as Viper's `Get` applies them and mapstructure's weak decode over the Go types of `config.Configuration`, with the account modules hook.

restorations.note: Each cast Viper's `Get` applies, against spf13/cast's own results.
Every input kind into every target kind, against mapstructure's own results.

differences.title: Set-Cookie attribute order: `http.Cookie` and the cookie crate write the same attributes in different orders
differences.go: `http.Cookie.String` writes `uids=eyJ1aWRzIjp7fX0=; Path=/; Domain=pbs.example; Expires=Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:20:30 GMT; Secure; SameSite=None` (usersync/cookie.go:93-113).
differences.rust: The cookie crate writes the same attributes and value, the base64 padding raw, in another order: `uids=eyJ1aWRzIjp7fX0=; SameSite=None; Secure; Path=/; Domain=pbs.example; Expires=Wed, 18 Nov 2026 10:20:30 GMT`.
differences.visible_in: The Set-Cookie header that writes the uids cookie (/setuid and /optout)
differences.note: The cookie's value, the uids JSON in base64, keeps Go's format under Rule B (b), and the harness compares it as JSON after base64 decoding.

differences.title: Gzip bytes: compress/gzip and flate2 write different deflate streams of the same payload
differences.go: `compress/gzip` at the default level writes Go's deflate stream, and its `Close` adds an empty stored block: 129 bytes for the pinned bid request (exchange/bidder.go:848-880).
differences.rust: flate2 (miniz_oxide) writes another valid stream, 128 bytes for the same request, with the same 10-byte header (`1f 8b 08 00`, MTIME 0, XFL 0, OS 255). Both inflate to the same bytes; a bidder sees other compressed bytes and another Content-Length.
differences.visible_in: The bodies and Content-Length of bidder requests sent with `endpoint_compression: gzip`

differences.title: Default Accept: reqwest sends `Accept: */*`, net/http sends none
differences.go: `net/http` adds no `Accept`, so the currency and vendor-list GETs and the adapter requests that set none carry no `Accept` (currency/rate_converter.go:53).
differences.rust: reqwest 0.13.5's `ClientBuilder::new` puts `Accept: */*` among the client's default headers, so every request without an `Accept` of its own carries it; a caller's `Accept` replaces it.
differences.visible_in: Outbound requests whose caller set no Accept
differences.restore: None in reqwest's API: `ClientBuilder::default_headers` only adds to the defaults and cannot drop one. Accepted under Rule A (orchestrator ruling 9); HTTP-CLIENT may add a crate-level pin.

differences.title: Default User-Agent: net/http sends `Go-http-client/1.1`, reqwest sends none
differences.go: `net/http` sends `User-Agent: Go-http-client/1.1` when the caller set none.
differences.rust: reqwest sends no `User-Agent` at all.
differences.visible_in: Outbound requests whose caller set no User-Agent: bidder requests without one, and the currency and vendor-list fetches
differences.restore: HTTP-CLIENT sets `Go-http-client/1.1` when the caller set none, one line of client config (D-UA, orchestrator ruling 5), and HTTP-H2 keeps it on HTTP/2.

differences.title: Control characters: jsoniter writes `\u0008` and `\u000c`, encoding/json and serde_json `\b` and `\f`
differences.go: jsoniter (`jsonutil.Marshal`) writes U+0008 and U+000C as `\u0008` and `\u000c`; `json.Marshal` and the endpoints' Encoders (Go 1.22 and later) write `\b` and `\f`. The other control characters are `\u00XX` in all of them, and DEL is written as it is.
differences.rust: serde_json writes `\b` and `\f`, as `encoding/json` does; the other control characters are `\u00XX`, and DEL is written as it is.
differences.visible_in: Strings holding U+0008 or U+000C in what `jsonutil.Marshal` wrote: ext members, adapter request bodies and cache payloads
differences.note: Its mismatches are lexical `unicode_escape`, which the pattern of `json.html-escape` takes everywhere, so the harness counts them there: one pattern per class and path.

differences.title: Duplicate JSON keys: Go keeps the last, the serde derives reject the document
differences.go: jsoniter and `encoding/json` keep the last of duplicate keys.
differences.rust: The serde derives reject the document (`duplicate field`); a `serde_json::Value` keeps the last key, as Go does.
differences.visible_in: The status of requests whose JSON repeats a key, and the handling of such bidder responses
differences.restore: Decode again through `serde_json::Value` on that error, the last key winning; not planned (D-DECODE).

differences.title: Float spelling: Go writes `1`, `300` and `1e-07` where serde_json writes `1.0`, `300.0` and `1e-7`
differences.go: strconv's shortest form, plain for `1e-6 <= |f| < 1e21` (1e20 is `100000000000000000000`) and with an exponent otherwise, which jsoniter (`jsonutil.Marshal`) writes `1e-07` and `encoding/json` (`json.Marshal` in 222 adapter files, the endpoints' Encoders) `1e-7`. A float32 is written at 32 bits, an integral value has no fraction (`1`, `300`) and -0 stays `-0`. A number read into `interface{}` is a float64: `12345678901234567890` comes back as `12345678901234567000`, and `300.0` and `1E2` as `300` and `100`.
differences.rust: serde_json writes `1.0`, `300.0`, `123456789.0` and `1e+20`; an f64 0.000001 is `1e-6` and an f32 one `0.000001`, and -0 is `-0.0`. A `serde_json::Value` keeps integers exact and floats as f64: `300.0`, `100.0`, `1e-6`, `-0.0`.
differences.visible_in: Prices and other floats in response bodies, bidder request bodies, analytics and cache payloads
differences.restore: A serde_json Formatter overriding `write_f64` and `write_f32`; not planned (orchestrator ruling 2).
differences.note: Floats Prebid prints into its own text (targeting values, macros) use the precision Prebid's Go code uses, which is Prebid logic ported in place (orchestrator ruling 4), not this entry.

differences.title: HTML escaping: Go writes `<`, `>` and `&` as `\u` escapes, serde_json as they are
differences.go: `jsonutil.Marshal` (jsoniter's `ConfigCompatibleWithStandardLibrary`), `json.Marshal` and Encoders with default settings write `<`, `>` and `&` in strings as `\u003c`, `\u003e` and `\u0026`, and U+2028 and U+2029 as `\u2028` and `\u2029`. Inside a `json.RawMessage` only `json.Marshal` and such Encoders escape: `jsonutil.Marshal` writes one through the `RawMessageExtension` main.go:23-25 registers, which compacts it and escapes nothing (`json.raw-not-compacted`). The endpoints' Encoders turn HTML escaping off (`SetEscapeHTML(false)` at endpoints/openrtb2/auction.go:384, endpoints/openrtb2/amp_auction.go:408, endpoints/cookie_sync.go:561 and exchange/exchange.go:986) and still escape U+2028 and U+2029 in strings.
differences.rust: serde_json writes all five characters as they are. Strings the endpoints' Encoders write themselves, such as a bid's `adm`, differ only in U+2028 and U+2029; the `<`, `>` and `&` differences sit in what `jsonutil.Marshal` and `json.Marshal` wrote: ext members, adapter request bodies and cache payloads.
differences.visible_in: Response bodies, bidder request bodies and Prebid Cache payloads
differences.restore: A serde_json Formatter that adds Go's escapes; not planned (D-HTMLESC).
differences.note: The `unicode_escape` pattern also takes the control-character spellings of `json.control-escapes`.

differences.title: Invalid UTF-8 in JSON strings: Go decodes it, serde_json rejects the document
differences.go: jsoniter (`jsonutil.Unmarshal` and `UnmarshalValid`) keeps an invalid byte as it came (`a`, 0xFF, `b` stays `61ff62`); only `encoding/json`'s `json.Unmarshal` writes U+FFFD (`61efbfbd62`).
differences.rust: The serde derives reject the document (`invalid unicode code point`).
differences.visible_in: The status of requests whose JSON strings hold bytes that are not UTF-8, and the handling of such bidder responses
differences.restore: Replace invalid sequences with U+FFFD and decode again, which is `encoding/json`'s result (a Rust String cannot hold jsoniter's raw byte); not planned (D-DECODE).

differences.title: JSON keys: Go matches struct fields ignoring case, serde matches exactly
differences.go: jsoniter (`jsonutil.Unmarshal`, `UnmarshalValid`) and `encoding/json` match object keys to struct fields ignoring case, so `"ID"` fills `id`.
differences.rust: serde matches keys exactly; another spelling is an unknown key, ignored, and the field is defaulted or missing. A request whose imps are under `"Imp"` has no imps and gets a 400.
differences.visible_in: Requests and bidder responses whose keys differ in case from the field names: the status, or the values the field would have held
differences.restore: A decode pass that folds keys as jsoniter does; not planned (D-DECODE).

differences.title: Lone UTF-16 surrogate escapes: Go decodes them to U+FFFD, serde_json rejects the document
differences.go: jsoniter (`jsonutil.Unmarshal`, `UnmarshalValid`) and `encoding/json` decode a `\u` escape of a surrogate that forms no pair (a high surrogate before a letter, a low one alone, two high ones) to U+FFFD, once per lone surrogate, and the document decodes.
differences.rust: serde_json rejects the whole document, into the derives and into a `Value` alike.
differences.visible_in: Requests whose strings were cut inside an escaped emoji (Prebid.js sends `JSON.stringify` output, which writes a lone surrogate as `\uD83D`), which Go answers with 200 and serde_json would turn into a 400, and bidder responses with such strings
differences.restore: JSONUTIL's decode entry for outside bytes (request bodies, stored data, bidder responses: every place Go calls `jsonutil.Unmarshal` or `json.Unmarshal` on outside input) rewrites each unpaired `\uD800`-`\uDFFF` escape to `\uFFFD` before serde_json reads the bytes, scanning only when the bytes hold a `\u` escape of that range, with string and escape state tracked (orchestrator ruling 7).

differences.title: Nesting depth: Go reads 10000 levels, a `serde_json::Value` stops at 128
differences.go: jsoniter and `encoding/json` accept 10000 levels of nesting (9999 arrays inside the outer object) and reject a deeper document, whether the deep value lands in a `json.RawMessage`, in an `interface{}` or in a key they skip.
differences.rust: serde_json stops a `Value` at 128 levels, the outer object included (127 arrays inside it fail with `recursion limit exceeded`), and reads a `RawValue` or skips an unknown key at any depth, 10001 levels included.
differences.visible_in: The status of requests whose JSON nests 128 levels or more, and the handling of such bidder responses

differences.title: NaN and infinities: Go fails the write, serde_json writes `null`
differences.go: A NaN or infinite float, and a float32 that overflowed to +Inf, fails the marshal: `jsonutil.Marshal` returns `FailedToMarshal` with jsoniter's `unsupported value: NaN` after the field's path, and `encoding/json` returns `json: unsupported value: NaN`. The auction endpoint then records `/openrtb2/auction Failed to send response` among the analytics errors and sets the request status `RequestStatusNetworkErr`, and the response body is not written (endpoints/openrtb2/auction.go:394-397).
differences.rust: serde_json writes `null` in the value's place before any Formatter sees it, so the document goes out.
differences.visible_in: Response bodies, and the request status metric, when a float in the response is not finite
differences.restore: A `serialize_with` helper on every f32 and f64 field that fails as the Go writer does; not planned (orchestrator rulings 2 and 5).

differences.title: `null` for a value field: Go keeps the zero value, serde rejects the document
differences.go: `null` given to a field that is not a pointer or interface (a number, bool, string, struct, slice or map) leaves the field at its zero value, and the document decodes.
differences.rust: serde rejects the document (`invalid type: null`).
differences.visible_in: Requests and bidder responses that send `null` for a value field
differences.restore: JSONUTIL and ORTB-SERDE: container `#[serde(default)]` plus typegen's `null_default` deserializer on every value field, so a `null` leaves the default; real traffic sends these nulls.

differences.title: `json.RawMessage` on write: Go compacts it, serde_json writes a `RawValue` as it was read
differences.go: `jsonutil.Marshal` writes a `json.RawMessage` through Prebid's `RawMessageExtension` (registered at main.go:23-25), which runs `json.Compact`: whitespace goes, nothing is escaped, and for bytes that are not JSON nothing is written and no error returned, so the output (`{"id":"1","ext":}`) is not JSON. `json.Marshal` and the endpoints' Encoders compact it too, HTML-escaping inside it unless `SetEscapeHTML(false)`, and fail on bytes that are not JSON (`error calling MarshalJSON for type json.RawMessage: unexpected end of JSON input`).
differences.rust: A `RawValue` is written as it was read, whitespace included, and serde_json cannot build one from bytes that are not JSON.
differences.visible_in: Ext members and other raw JSON in bidder request bodies and in responses
differences.restore: JSONUTIL: `raw_compact`, the equivalent of Prebid's own `RawMessageExtension`, which typegen puts on every `json.RawMessage` field. This is Prebid logic, not library glue; the escaping inside stays `json.html-escape`.

differences.title: Log lines: glog's header with the facade's file and line, against tracing-subscriber's format
differences.go: glog writes `W1118 12:00:00.000000 4242 logger.go:17] message`: the level letter and the date, the time to the microsecond, the PID and the file and line, which through Prebid's logger facade (depth 1, logger/glog.go:37-41) are always the facade's own, `logger.go:17` for a warning.
differences.rust: tracing-subscriber's fmt layer writes `<RFC 3339 time>  WARN <module path>: message`: an RFC 3339 time, the level padded to five characters and the event's target, with no file or line.
differences.visible_in: The server's log output (stderr, as the image runs with `-logtostderr`)
differences.note: The glog calls that bypass the facade (the rules engine's observer.go:14 and :20, and the WURFL module) write their own file and line; no pin covers them.

differences.title: Prometheus sample values: client_golang writes `1e+06`, the prometheus crate `1000000`
differences.go: client_golang writes a sample with `strconv.FormatFloat(v, 'g', -1, 64)`: a counter at one million is `1e+06` and one at 123456789 is `1.23456789e+08`, while 100000 and 1 are written as they are.
differences.rust: The prometheus crate writes `1000000` and `123456789`. The HELP and TYPE lines and the label order are the same.
differences.visible_in: The /metrics exposition, for sample values of a million and above

differences.title: Public suffix lookups: x/net/publicsuffix fails on empty labels and IP addresses, psl answers
differences.go: `publicsuffix.EffectiveTLDPlusOne` (x/net v0.55.0) fails on a host with an empty label (a trailing dot, a leading dot, two dots in a row) and on a bare IP address, which `PublicSuffix` returns whole, so the auction leaves `site.publisher.domain` unset for such a referrer (endpoints/openrtb2/auction.go:1607-1611).
differences.rust: `psl::domain_str` answers `example.com` for `example.com.`, `www.example.com.` and `.example.com`, `.com` for `example..com`, `example.co.uk` for `a..b.example.co.uk` and `1.1` for `192.168.1.1`, so the domain is set. Both answer `1.1:8080` for `192.168.1.1:8080`, and neither finds a domain in `[::1]:8080`.
differences.visible_in: `site.publisher.domain` in bidder requests and analytics, for referrers whose host has an empty label or is an IPv4 address
differences.restore: Check the host for empty labels and parse it as an IP address before calling psl, leaving the domain unset where Go's lookup fails: glue under Rule B (a), for referrers production traffic sends that psl reads differently.
differences.default: psl's answer, so the domain is set where Go leaves it unset (crates first).

differences.title: `\Q...\E` literals: Go's regexp reads them, the regex crate rejects the pattern
differences.go: Go's `regexp` reads `\Q...\E` as a literal.
differences.rust: The regex crate rejects the pattern. No Prebid pattern uses it today.
differences.visible_in: Compiling a pattern that uses `\Q...\E`, which none of Prebid's patterns does
differences.restore: UTIL-CRATES: goregex rewrites `\Q...\E` as escaped literals in every pattern Prebid compiles.

differences.title: `\d`, `\w`, `\s` and `\b`: ASCII-only in Go's regexp, Unicode-aware in the regex crate
differences.go: `\d`, `\w`, `\s` and `\b` are ASCII-only in Go's `regexp`, and Go has no `(?-u)` flag.
differences.rust: The regex crate's classes are Unicode-aware unless the pattern says `(?-u:\d)`: Arabic-Indic digits, accented and CJK letters, a no-break space and an em space match where Go's do not, and `\b` sees no boundary between an accented letter and `foo`.
differences.visible_in: Bidder-params validation (static/bidder-params patterns such as visx's `^\d+$`), the adapters' patterns and the sync URL macros
differences.restore: UTIL-CRATES: `pbs_util::goregex` translates the classes, so Prebid's own patterns, in code and in static/bidder-params, keep Go's meaning.

differences.title: CORS on other requests: tower-http writes credentials on every answer, the origin for any method and a three-name Vary
differences.go: rs/cors, as `router.SupportCORS` configures it (router/router.go:377-385), writes `Vary: Origin` on every answer that is not a preflight, and `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` and `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` only when the request has an Origin and a method it allows (GET, POST and HEAD, and OPTIONS always); an OPTIONS without `Access-Control-Request-Method` goes on to the router.
differences.rust: tower-http's CorsLayer writes `access-control-allow-credentials: true` on every answer, server-to-server POSTs with no Origin included, `access-control-allow-origin` whatever the method (PUT too), and `vary: origin, access-control-request-method, access-control-request-headers`; it answers every OPTIONS itself as a preflight, so that request never reaches the handler.
differences.visible_in: The headers of every response
differences.note: These patterns also take the same headers of preflight answers (`server.cors-preflight`). Go's router answers an OPTIONS without `Access-Control-Request-Method` itself, with an `Allow` header (httprouter v1.3.0's router.go:422-425); the Rust server answers it as a preflight, so the `Allow` pattern takes that header, on OPTIONS cases only.

differences.title: CORS preflights: rs/cors answers 204 with the requested method and headers, tower-http 200 with its configured lists
differences.go: rs/cors answers a preflight with 204: `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` (the origin), `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`, `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` echoing the requested POST, `Access-Control-Allow-Headers` echoing the requested headers, and `Vary: Origin, Access-Control-Request-Method, Access-Control-Request-Headers`. When a requested header is not allowed (`x-custom`), it answers 204 with only that Vary.
differences.rust: tower-http's CorsLayer answers 200 every time, with `GET,POST,HEAD`, `origin,x-requested-with,content-type,accept` and a lower-case `vary`, a disallowed requested header included. The browser's verdict is the same in all three cases.
differences.visible_in: Answers to CORS preflights on every endpoint
differences.restore: A CORS layer of our own that answers as rs/cors does; not planned (orchestrator ruling 5 accepts and ledgers the difference).

differences.title: RFC 3339 times: Go's RFC3339 layout writes whole seconds, the time crate's `Rfc3339` the fraction
differences.go: The `time.RFC3339` layout writes whole seconds (`2026-11-18T10:20:30Z`), and `time.RFC3339Nano` the fraction without trailing zeros.
differences.rust: The time crate's well-known `Rfc3339` writes the fraction whenever there is one, as `RFC3339Nano` does, so whole seconds need a format description of their own.
differences.visible_in: Times Prebid formats with the RFC3339 layout, such as the last-modified parameter of stored-request event polling (stored_requests/events/http/http.go:127)
differences.restore: UTIL-CRATES: format descriptions for the RFC3339 and RFC3339Nano layouts Prebid's code picks. This is Prebid's formatting choice ported in place, as ruling 4 does for floats; the uids cookie's times are Rule B (b).

differences.title: URL hosts: Go's `url.Parse` keeps the host as written, the url crate normalises it
differences.go: `url.Parse` keeps `Host` as written (`Example.COM:80`) and a non-ASCII host as it came, which `String()` percent-encodes; `site.domain` takes the referrer's `Host`, port included (endpoints/openrtb2/auction.go:1606-1608).
differences.rust: The url crate (WHATWG) lower-cases the host, drops the scheme's default port and writes a non-ASCII host in IDNA form.
differences.visible_in: `site.domain` and the other values Prebid takes from a URL's host, in bidder requests
differences.restore: A Go-style URL parser for the URLs Prebid writes back; not planned (orchestrator rulings, 2026-11-19).

differences.title: YAML 1.1 booleans: yaml.v3 takes three spellings of each word, serde-saphyr any case
differences.go: yaml.v3 decodes into a `bool` only `y`, `Y`, `yes`, `Yes`, `YES`, `on`, `On`, `ON`, `true`, `True` and `TRUE`, and the false forms in the same spellings; mixed case (`yEs`, `oN`, `tRue`, `fAlse`) fails the load (config/bidderinfo.go:323).
differences.rust: serde-saphyr matches the words in any case, so a mixed-case value that fails Go's load loads here. `1`, `0`, `t` and `f` fail on both sides.
differences.visible_in: Startup with a bidder-info YAML file (static/bidder-info) that spells a boolean in mixed case

differences.title: YAML parse errors: yaml.v3 and serde-saphyr word them differently
differences.go: yaml.v3 v3.0.1 words its errors as `yaml: line 2: found character that cannot start any token` or `yaml: unmarshal errors:` with the lines below it.
differences.rust: serde-saphyr words them its own way, with the line and column, as `tabs disallowed within this context (block indentation) at line 2, column 2`; the same documents fail.
differences.visible_in: Nowhere: Prebid drops the error of a pbs.yaml that does not parse (config/config.go:1322), and only the verdict, which is the same, shows
differences.restore: Port yaml.v3's scanner and its messages; not planned.

differences.title: YAML scalars: yaml.v3 and serde-saphyr resolve some plain scalars to different types
differences.go: yaml.v3 v3.0.1 parses integers with `strconv.ParseInt` base 0, so `0X1F`, `0O17`, `0B101`, `1_` and `1__0` are numbers, and floats after removing underscores (`1_000.5`); it keeps an out-of-range float such as `1e400` a string, makes YAML 1.1 timestamps such as `2001-12-14` `time.Time` (a string key then gets `2001-12-14 00:00:00 +0000 UTC`), keeps the text of a scalar with a custom tag, and fails on `!!null x`.
differences.rust: serde-saphyr keeps those numbers and timestamps strings, reads `1e400` as infinity, resolves a scalar with a custom tag as if untagged (`!e!x 1` is the number 1) and reads `!!null x` as null.
differences.visible_in: Startup with a pbs.yaml that writes such a scalar; none of the 398 bidder-info files of the pinned upstream does
differences.restore: Resolve plain scalars from serde-saphyr's events with yaml.v3's rules; not planned.
